reviewer: Independent Codex GATE: bounded one-off reviewed-token pipe launcher
objective: Independently review only execute_reviewed_cutover.py and its focused synthetic handoff tests before separate operation/tool approval. No credential retrieval or cutover execution by reviewer.
scope: One bridge from the exact original running orchestrator SERVICE_TOKEN to the unchanged reviewed cutover.main through an owned anonymous pipe, using the existing validated input set and controller600/recovery180 budgets.
shown: The source is inert without --execute-once. Its default path validates pinned public inputs and prints only a fixed nonexecuting summary; neither execute(), Docker inspection nor token access is invoked.

RECEIPT_SHA, SCOPE_SHA and RUNTIME_SHA match the saved inert validation receipt and independently accepted records. inputs() rehashes the reviewed scripts/research consumers, accepts only the exact frozen env-i/Python/module command prefix, and refuses execution/token switches in the base argv. It uses shlex parsing, not shell execution of the receipt.

execute() disables core dumps before loading inputs, changes to the fixed repository root and calls the existing cutover.load_inputs on the fixed parsed arguments before any credential-source operation.

Credential selection is the original phase1-orchestrator in plan.baseline, not the staged replacement. The inspect template requires its exact full container ID, exact image ID and running state before returning only SERVICE_TOKEN entries as JSON strings. No exchange credential/API-key/password field, broad environment output or alternate token source is requested.

The planned source read uses the pinned Docker CLI, fixed Unix endpoint, empty temporary Docker config, PATH-only child environment, a10second CLI-verification deadline, a separate at-most10second inspect and8192byte stdout bound. stdout remains in Python memory; stderr is discarded by the existing transport. No token file, hash, length, argv or environment export is authored.

parse_token requires bytes, at most8192 raw bytes, exactly one nonempty JSON-framed row, the exact SERVICE_TOKEN= prefix and a nonempty printable-ASCII payload of at most4096characters. Missing, duplicated, wrong-prefix, whitespace/control/non-ASCII or malformed values refuse without fallback.

handoff() creates its own anonymous pipe, refuses a read descriptor<=2, makes the writer nonblocking, performs one checked complete write and closes the writer before invoking the entrypoint. EOF terminates the existing token reader; the token is not added to argv, only the descriptor number.

The unchanged cutover.main accepts descriptor ownership; its finally closes an unconsumed supplied descriptor on ordinary handled failures, and token_from_pipe consumes/closes it after bounded validation. The fixed argv is accepted by the same argument grammar before transfer. No controller, retry, recovery, start/stop policy or parent kill-timer code is changed.

The launcher makes one cutover.main call with --execute-cutover and --token-fd appended. It adds no retry/fallback/recovery path; the existing lock/reservation/one-shot and owned rollback logic remain authoritative.

Failures handled by execute() print fixed JSON only, not the exception payload, source stdout, token value or traceback. Local token/raw/payload references are cleared when their scopes end; this is reference clearing, not forensic memory erasure.

findings.subject: Diagnostic entered flag is broader than consumer entry
findings.detail: entered=True is assigned immediately before handoff(). A pipe allocation/write/descriptor failure can therefore emit entrypoint_handoff_entered=true even though cutover.main was never invoked.
findings.disposition: Accepted diagnostic risk, not execution authority or a safety-guard bypass. Treat the flag only as producer handoff-attempt progress; use the unchanged cutover receipt/actions_executed/attempt-reservation evidence to establish actual consumer entry and operations.

verification.environment: VERIFIED_ENV for isolated focused synthetic host tests, local public-input hashes and AST-isolated fake-descriptor assertions only
verification.focused_command: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 ./.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest --noconftest -c /dev/null -p no:cacheprovider -q --tb=short tests/test_companion_reviewed_cutover_handoff.py
verification.focused_result: 13 passed in0.18s against the final reviewed source including the descriptor guard
verification.additional_command: /usr/bin/python3 -B - <<'PY' (standard-library source/hash assertions and isolated handoff AST with fake OS descriptors)
verification.additional_result: PASS: exact pinned inert receipt/scope/runtime/consumer hashes; original orchestrator baseline selected; three synthetic pre-handoff descriptor failures refuse before invoke and close both owned ends
verification.synthetic_success: Focused test sends only a synthetic token through a local owned pipe to the existing token_from_pipe reader, sees EOF and returns once; no real token or service call.
verification.synthetic_rejections: Focused tests cover missing/malformed/wrong-prefix/empty/space/newline/duplicate/oversized/non-ASCII source payloads. Additional fake-OS checks cover fd<=2, short write and would-block before callback invocation.

limits: The Go template was source-reviewed, not executed against a credential source by this GATE. Runtime source-ID/image/running mismatch, CLI verification failure, absent/duplicate/unsupported token or pipe failure must refuse; successful live handoff is not claimed.

The token remains in process memory during handoff and the owning runtime's authorized use. Core dumps are disabled, but immutable strings/bytes are not zeroized; process-memory secrecy is not a forensic guarantee.

The helper is reviewed only with the exact hash-bound cutover.main callback and validated argv. It is not a general descriptor-transfer API: ownership is relinquished immediately before callback invocation, so an arbitrary callback that never assumes ownership would not be covered.

Before the unchanged cutover entrypoint installs its handlers, the launcher adds no new cancellation/recovery machinery. Interruption in this pre-entry credential/pipe phase is not a claim of an owned rollback; no application mutation is authored in that phase.

The producer does not reserve the cutover attempt before reading the token. Reinvocation can repeat the source read before the existing consumer lock/attempt marker refuses reuse; --execute-once is an explicit invocation switch, not a separate producer one-use journal. No automatic retry is present or accepted.

The prelude CLI verification/inspect is separately bounded; no claim that all local I/O or the entire launcher fits inside the consumer's600second controller budget is made. The600/180 consumer budgets are unchanged.

Existing policy/source/configuration/identity/recipient/namespace/citation checks, allowed audit writes, preserved storage and owned rollback requirements remain unchanged. This review is not evidence that the future operation or rollback succeeds.
No secret-source fallback, exchange/API credential discovery, source rebuild, SDK initialization or unreviewed runtime criterion is authorized.
Only runtime_packet/reviewed_handoff_review.json is written. Parent owns the operation authorization record and tool approval; reviewed launcher/tests/consumers and earlier receipts are preserved.
acceptance_boundary: Technical launcher review accepted with the stated risks. Any operation must remain the separately authorized exact one-attempt four-application cutover plus one archived query, with original storage preserved and existing controller-owned recovery; this GATE performs none of it.
